problem: "A loop that never changes its condition is infinite" is misleading: the condition text ($i <= 5) never changes; what must change is the variable inside it. A student may read this as "the condition must be rewritten each pass".
fix: A loop whose condition never becomes false is infinite, because nothing inside the body moves the test toward false. Example: for ($i = 1; $i <= 5; ) with no $i++ runs forever.

problem: The sentence "PHP stops at max_execution_time" is only true for web requests. Under the command line, max_execution_time defaults to 0, meaning no time limit, so a student testing an infinite loop in the terminal sees it run forever.
fix: In a web request PHP stops the script when max_execution_time (default 30 seconds) is exceeded. In CLI this limit is 0 by default, so the loop keeps running until you stop it with Ctrl+C.

problem: "Remove the & after the loop" is not an operation a student can perform; the & lives in the foreach header. The leftover reference is removed by unsetting the loop variable, as the trap later says.
fix: The loop variable is a copy; changing it does not change the array unless you write foreach ($a as &$value). After such a loop, call unset($value) so the reference does not silently overwrite the last element later.

problem: "It visits each key => value pair once" is stated before the two forms are introduced, so a beginner reading foreach ($a as $v) may expect a key to be available. The plain form gives values only.
fix: foreach ($a as $v) gives each value in turn, in insertion order; foreach ($a as $k => $v) gives the key and the value together.
